title: Capture official inactives from club news feeds
problem: The availability graph is blocked because no inactive list has ever been read, yet the route is now proven
option_a: Ad hoc: fetch each club's Week N inactives article by hand each week
option_b: Scheduled: a daily job that lists club news feeds and stores any article whose title matches inactives
option_c: Skip inactives and treat the game designation as the outcome
recommendation: Option B, piloted on 3 clubs for one week before scaling to 32
what_would_change_the_call: If fewer than 20 of 32 clubs publish inactives within 90 minutes of kickoff, fall back to A

title: Capture official snap counts from club game books
problem: Depth is currently modelled from club charts, which several clubs label unofficial; the brief demands playing time
option_a: Scrape the club Gamebook article for participation
option_b: Use the NFL game book PDF endpoint if one is reachable
option_c: Model depth from charts and publish a caveat on every row
recommendation: Option A, piloted on one game book; if it carries no snap counts, do C and flag it
what_would_change_the_call: If no official snap-count source exists for any club, formally adopt C and record the limitation on the deficiency page

title: Automate the injury-report capture on a Wednesday-Friday cadence
problem: Two reads exist, both made by hand, so the injury series cannot be replayed
option_a: Write a scheduled job that fetches the league injury page daily and stores raw text with a hash
option_b: Pay a data vendor for a historical designation feed
option_c: Keep manual reads and accept that the series is incomplete
recommendation: Option A; it is cheap and it is the only route that also builds the archive the brief requires
what_would_change_the_call: If the league blocks automated access, escalate to B

title: Resolve the Houston depth chart
problem: One of 32 clubs is invisible to the deficiency matrix
option_a: Test the club's JSON endpoints for a structured chart
option_b: Use the league's own depth endpoint if it exists
option_c: Ask the club's media-relations desk for a structured feed
recommendation: Try A then B; only use C if both fail. Never transcribe the image by eye
what_would_change_the_call: If a structured source appears for Houston, drop C immediately

title: Capture the league transactions and reserve lists
problem: Not listed cannot be distinguished from healthy, and stale depth rows cannot be proven stale
option_a: Fetch the league transactions page daily and diff against depth rows
option_b: Track reserve moves from club news pages only
option_c: Do nothing and label every absence as unknown
recommendation: A, then join to depth rows to flag staleness automatically
what_would_change_the_call: If the transactions page does not carry reserve designations, add B

title: Decide the price-data policy before the first backtest
problem: A residual against the market cannot be published because no market price exists
option_b: Capture two or more and build a vig-free consensus
option_c: Publish our own line only and never claim a residual
recommendation: A then B: one operator first, consensus second, because the decomposition in R-60 needs the margin
what_would_change_the_call: If the operator terms forbid storage, stop and re-open this decision before capturing anything

title: Store prices on a fixed schedule, not on demand
problem: Price snapshots need an opening and a closing number, which needs a schedule
option_a: Capture twice daily: on publication and 90 minutes before kickoff
recommendation: B; the close is what CLV is graded against, and the open is what makes the move visible
what_would_change_the_call: If storage cost becomes material, drop to A

title: Promote the suggestions page to the top-level navigation
problem: Suggestions exist but a reviewer has to know to look for them
option_a: Put Suggestions and Questions in the primary nav on every page
option_b: Keep them as subpages and link from the landing page only
option_c: Merge them into one review page
recommendation: Option A; the brief asks for a dedicated, reviewable section
what_would_change_the_call: None; this is a presentation choice, reversible at any time

title: Add a decision log that records each review decision and its date
problem: Suggestions carry a status but no history of who decided what
option_a: Append a dated row to a decision log whenever a status changes
option_b: Use git history as the decision log
recommendation: Option A; a reviewer needs the decision and its date together, not spread across commits

title: Consolidate the eleven NFL desks behind one index
problem: Four namespaces now answer the same brief, so a reviewer cannot tell which is current
option_a: Build a desks index page listing every namespace with its as-of date and scope
option_b: Nominate one desk as canonical and archive the rest
recommendation: Option A first; it is additive and needs no one to give up a scope
what_would_change_the_call: If an integration session is scheduled, defer to it and do B there

title: Keep both total estimators until a walk-forward separates them
problem: The brief asks for two estimators and a gap column; collapsing early would repeat a documented leakage error
option_a: Publish both and compare weekly on chronological holdouts
option_b: Collapse to the better in-sample estimator now
recommendation: B; the first totals walk-forward in this repo leaked and was corrected, so the comparison must be chronological and out-of-sample
what_would_change_the_call: If the gap stays inside its own standard error for 6 weeks, collapse to the simpler estimator

title: Promote the ratings model only after an opponent-aware backtest
problem: Ratings are fitted on one season and ridge-penalised, which is necessary but not yet validated
option_a: Backtest the ratings on chronological holdouts once 2+ seasons exist
option_b: Ship week-11 lines now as PAPER and backtest later
option_c: Both: publish PAPER now, backtest on the schedule
recommendation: Option C; publishing is free once nothing is certified, and the backtest gate cannot clear on one season
what_would_change_the_call: If the holdout shows the ratings are worse than the market baseline, demote to a baseline only

title: Keep every division empty until its gate clears
problem: Ranking before the gates clear would make the leaderboard noise
option_a: Publish the divisions with zero rows and the gate that blocks each
option_c: Hide the leaderboard until it has rows
recommendation: Option A; an empty table with the blocking gate is more honest than a rank

title: Fund the reward pool only after G1 clears
problem: Reward amounts are currently blank by policy
option_a: Leave the pool blank and publish the gate that unlocks it
option_b: Set a notional pool now for motivation
recommendation: Option A or D (non-cash badges) while G1 is unmet; a funded pool before 300 graded bets would pay for variance
what_would_change_the_call: If a sponsor requires a published figure before results exist, use D

title: Publish the injury delta as the feature, never the level
problem: A level tells you a player is hurt; a delta tells you something changed this week
option_a: Delta only, with the level shown beside it for context
recommendation: Option A; the brief is explicit, and the level is kept only as context
what_would_change_the_call: If the delta series proves to have no signal on outcomes, revisit

title: Separate the reward decision from the ranking decision
problem: One decision (who wins) is being asked to settle another (what the prize is)
option_a: Two entries in the decision log, two dates
recommendation: Option A; a prize decided after seeing ranks invites result-chasing

title: Move raw captures out of the public site
problem: The brief asks for a public analysis layer and a private data layer; raw captures are currently published
option_a: Create a private store and keep only derived analysis public
option_c: Publish raw captures but strip player names
recommendation: Option A; it matches the brief and removes the only plausible terms-of-use exposure
what_would_change_the_call: If legal review clears redistribution, B is acceptable

title: Add a drift alarm to every parser before automating capture
problem: Without pins, an automated scraper can silently publish blanks
option_a: Pin row counts and required fields, and fail the build loudly when a field goes missing
option_b: Automate capture first and add pins later
recommendation: Option A; the brief asks for the alarm before the automation, and this session's Houston and Packers findings are exactly the failures the pins would have caught
